turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before they did.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. And Owen found out from his phone, in the middle of a class. What happens to the zero now, Hale?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Show me the page, Hale. I'm writing down the line and I'll check it myself. A wrong quotation in a Grade 12 essay is a mistake in the essay, so what else do you have?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, Hale, and the principal will see it in my email.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that you should have called me before entering the zero, and you apologised. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that you retract your remark that something "seems to run in the family." I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, and she agreed to nothing.
What moved her: nothing.
